unit1.title: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the primary focus of technical communication, in contrast to academic writing?

options.A: Personal thoughts and feelings of the writer
options.B: Showing mastery of a body of information

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four basic communication skills mentioned for technical communication?

options.B: Speaking

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the main purpose of technical communication?

options.A: To create new knowledge for a general audience
options.B: To reinforce or change attitudes, motivate actions, or help readers with work-related tasks
options.C: To get a good grade from an instructor
options.D: To express personal experiences and opinions

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: A public-health scientist creating a journal article, a press release, and a blog post about the same study is an example of tailoring content for what?

options.B: The required length of the document

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Technical communication is defined as the exchange of information that helps people interact with what?

options.B: Technology and solve complex problems

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of technical documents regarding their audience?

options.A: They focus on the writer's personal thoughts
options.B: They are reader-centered, with the needs of the readers coming first
options.C: They are written to impress critics
options.D: They are always highly technical and complex

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which feature of an accessible and efficient technical document involves using heads, lists, and white space?

options.B: Readable style

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Who is typically involved in creating complex technical documents?

options.B: A single subject matter expert
options.C: Teams composed of various professionals like writers, engineers, and managers

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of technical writing?

options.B: Communicates complex information clearly, concisely, and accurately
options.D: Is only delivered in digital format

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is one of the key characteristics of technical writing?

options.B: Wordy

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Why is technical writing considered a "foundational professional skill" and not a "soft skill" for engineers?

options.A: It is only required for senior-level roles
options.B: It directly impacts the quality of their work and is a business imperative
options.C: It is a skill you are born with
options.D: It is only used for internal communication

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of an Engineering Notebook or Logbook?

options.B: To protect intellectual property and provide a historical record of the design process
options.D: To serve as a rough draft for a final report

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the goal of an internal memo or email within a company?

options.B: To convey information quickly and efficiently to colleagues

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the primary audience for a user manual?

options.B: Investors
options.C: End-users who may not have a technical background

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Strong writing skills are a prerequisite for which type of roles?

options.B: Internships
options.C: Senior roles like Project Manager or Team Lead

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is described as the "ethical responsibility" of an engineer regarding technical documents?

options.B: To ensure documents are entertaining
options.C: To provide clear instructions to prevent accidents and real-world consequences
options.D: To use as much jargon as possible

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What are the four pillars of effective technical communication?

options.B: Clarity, conciseness, accuracy, and audience focus

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the meaning of Clarity in technical communication?

options.B: The quality of being easy to understand, with an unmistakable message
options.D: Using a formal tone at all times

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the "inverted pyramid" style of writing?

options.A: Starting with a detailed introduction and ending with a brief conclusion
options.B: Beginning with the least important information and building up to the main point
options.C: Starting with the most important information first

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Why is Accuracy considered "non-negotiable" in engineering communication?

options.A: Inaccurate data can make a document look unprofessional
options.B: It is a matter of personal pride for the writer
options.C: Mistakes can lead to serious consequences like structural failure or user injury
options.D: It is required by law in most countries

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of an Audience and Purpose Analysis?

options.B: To identify readers' characteristics and define the document's goal
options.C: To find out what the writer already knows
options.D: To avoid having to cite sources

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Who belongs to the "Primary audience" for a technical document?

options.B: Auditors and future employees
options.C: The direct recipients who use the document to make decisions or take action

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Who is part of the "Secondary audience"?

options.B: Reviewers or advisors who evaluate the document for accuracy and quality

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the main characteristic of the "Tertiary audience"?

options.B: They are the primary financial backers
options.C: They interact with the document indirectly for reference or archival purposes

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four phases of the technical communication process?

options.B: Drafting

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the main goal of the Planning phase?

options.A: To start writing as fast as possible
options.B: To perfect the grammar and spelling
options.C: To define the audience, purpose, and scope before writing

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the primary mindset for the Drafting phase?

options.B: Turn off the inner editor and focus on capturing the core message

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What does "Revision" mean in the context of technical writing?

options.B: Looking at the big picture of the document for clarity and flow

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of the "Editing" phase?

options.B: To generate new content
options.C: To fine-tune the details, checking for grammar, spelling, and consistency
options.D: To define the audience and purpose

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a "portable skill" that employers seek in college graduates?

options.A: The ability to program in any language
options.B: The ability to get along with and motivate others
options.C: Mastery of a single, highly specialized software

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the main difference between academic writing and technical communication?

options.B: Technical communication has a different focus on audience and purpose
options.C: Academic writing is done in teams

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is a potential consequence of an engineer failing to communicate effectively?

options.B: Delays in project timelines

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Design Specification document?

options.A: To showcase the aesthetics of a product
options.B: To define what a product or system must do
options.C: To provide a list of project team members

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is a key skill for a technical writer creating presentations and slide decks?

options.B: Translating technical jargon into visual and verbal narratives

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the goal of a Client Report?

options.A: To persuade the client to cancel the project
options.B: To update the client on progress and justify design choices
options.C: To provide a history of the company
options.D: To critique the client's business model

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Why is it important to "read critically"?

options.A: To find mistakes in other people's writing
options.B: To learn what makes a document good or bad
options.D: To avoid writing your own documents

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What does the technical communication suggest you should do to achieve conciseness?

options.B: Eliminate wordy phrases and redundant information
options.C: Repeat your main points multiple times
options.D: Use a thesaurus to find longer words

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of citing sources in a technical document?

options.A: To make the document look longer
options.B: To give credit to the original research or data and ensure accuracy
options.D: To show off your research skills

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is a key question to ask when analyzing your audience?

options.B: What is my favorite color?
options.C: How familiar might the audience be with technical details?
options.D: How long will it take to write the document?

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is a key skill for writing effective emails and internal memos?

options.B: Using vague subject lines
options.C: Writing clear subject lines and structuring information logically

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Technical writing is a "tool" for engineers. What does this analogy mean?

options.A: It is only used for very specific tasks
options.B: It is a skill that can be mastered to make you a more effective engineer
options.C: It is a temporary skill that will become obsolete
options.D: It is a manual process that cannot be automated

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the benefit of a "sensible organization" in a technical document?

options.A: It makes the document look professional
options.B: It guides the reader and emphasizes important material
options.C: It allows the writer to express their feelings
options.D: It is a requirement for all documents

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Test Plan & Report?

options.A: To provide a financial breakdown of the project
options.B: To verify that the design meets its requirements and provides data for future improvements
options.C: To list all the team members
options.D: To explain how to use the final product

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: A good technical document presents content in "short chunks" and avoids "long technical passages" to be what?

options.B: More efficient and accessible

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an unethical communication?

options.B: Using a direct and simple tone
options.C: Inefficient style that confuses or misleads the audience

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Project Proposal?

options.B: To secure funding and justify resource allocation
options.C: To provide a list of materials used

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the goal of academic papers and conference proceedings?

options.B: To share research findings and establish credibility within the engineering community

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: Why is it important to "Embrace Feedback" on your writing?

options.A: It shows you are not a good writer
options.B: It is a requirement for all technical writers
options.C: To learn from your mistakes and improve
options.D: To get others to do your work for you

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the recommended style for a technical document?

options.B: A style that promotes fluid reading and accurate understanding
options.C: A style that uses as many literary devices as possible
options.D: A style that focuses on the writer's personal feelings

questions.unitName: Unit I: Introduction to Technical Communication
questions.question: What is the role of digital technology in technical communication?

options.A: It has made communication less frequent
options.B: It has provided more ways to research and find information
options.C: It has eliminated the need for critical thinking
options.D: It has made professional standards for communication obsolete

unit2.title: Unit II: The Research Process & Technical Evaluation

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: Major decisions in the workplace are based on what?

options.B: Careful research with findings recorded in a report

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the first procedural stage of the research process?

options.B: Writing the document

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: The stages of critical thinking in the research process begin with what action?

options.B: Asking the right questions

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: The answers you uncover will only be as good as the:

options.B: Time you spend

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What does critical thinking help a researcher to do with essential questions?

options.B: Define and refine them

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the key to solving a problem in research?

options.B: Avoiding a range of views

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: Ethical researchers rely on evidence that represents what?

options.B: The most comforting answer

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: Balanced research examines a broad range of evidence, while thorough research examines that evidence in:

options.B: A biased manner

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the main goal when evaluating your sources?

options.A: Emphasizing findings that support your own biases
options.B: Seeking out and reporting the most accurate answer

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: When interpreting findings, the document advises against forcing a simplistic conclusion on a complex issue, stating that a wrong conclusion is:

options.B: Far worse than no definite conclusion at all

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: Primary research is defined as getting information directly from the source by what methods?

options.B: Conducting interviews and surveys

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is secondary research?

options.B: Information obtained firsthand
options.C: Information obtained second hand by reading what other researchers have compiled
options.D: Information from an experiment you conducted

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: Most information found on the Internet is considered a:

options.B: Tertiary source

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: You should typically start your research with which type of source?

options.B: Secondary sources

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: How can working with primary sources add to the credibility of your work?

options.A: They are readily available and simple to use.
options.B: They help you expand upon what others have learned and add your own findings.
options.C: They are always more accurate than secondary sources.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of a subject directory?

options.A: It is a search engine that scans for keywords.
options.B: It is a list of Web sites compiled by editors.
options.C: It is a forum for discussion.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of search engines like Google and Yahoo!?

options.A: They are indexes compiled by editors.
options.B: They scan for Web sites that best match your query.
options.C: They are exclusively used for academic research.
options.D: They always provide the final, accurate word on a topic.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: You should use a Wikipedia entry for what purpose?

options.A: As your final destination for information.
options.B: To get an overview of a topic and locate other sources.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is "gray literature"?

options.A: Published books found in a library.
options.B: Information that is unpublished or not typically cataloged, like pamphlets or unpublished government documents.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a caution about using gray literature?

options.A: It is always carefully scrutinized for content by editors.
options.B: It is always a primary source.
options.C: It can be unreliable and should be backed up by information from other sources.
options.D: It is only available to experts.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is "source bias"?

options.A: A source that always reports the ultimate truth.
options.B: When a source understates or overstates certain facts depending on whose interests it represents.
options.D: A source that has been peer-reviewed.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What are the three distinct levels of certainty research can yield?

options.B: The ultimate truth, the probable answer, and the inconclusive answer

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is an assumption?

options.A: A notion that has been proven to be true.
options.B: An idea we accept without proof.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the process of rewriting a passage in your own words to make it shorter while still retaining its essential message?

options.B: Quoting

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the process of a restatement, in your own words, of someone else’s words?

options.B: Summarizing

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: When must you use quotation marks in your notes?

options.B: When you summarize a passage.
options.C: When you copy someone else's words, even a mere two or three in a row.
options.D: Only when you quote a full paragraph.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a key reason for taking notes accurately?

options.A: To avoid getting a grade of C.
options.B: To ensure you can plagiarize without being caught.
options.C: To prevent unintentional plagiarism and ensure the quality of your finished product.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: You can use a Wikipedia entry to get an overview of a topic and what else?

options.B: Locate other, more reliable sources.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What does it mean for research to be "reliable"?

options.A: It produces findings that can be replicated.
options.B: It is published in a book.
options.D: It is conducted by a well-known person.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: To what does the term "relevance" refer in the context of research depth?

options.A: The number of sources you find.
options.B: The quality and pertinence of the information you find.
options.C: The ease of finding information online.
options.D: The speed at which you conduct your search.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the primary function of documentation?

options.A: To make your document look more professional.
options.B: To help you acknowledge your debt to sources, establish credibility, and help readers find your sources.
options.D: To avoid having to write your own words.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: The failure to document a source, whether intentional or unintentional, is called:

options.B: Quoting

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What three kinds of material should always be documented?

options.B: Quotations, paraphrased ideas, and graphics.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: In APA style, for material that you have summarized or paraphrased, what must you include in the parentheses immediately following the borrowed information?

options.A: The author's name and the publication date.
options.B: The title and page number.
options.C: The author's last name and page number.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: When citing a source with three to five authors for the first time in APA style, what should you do?

options.B: Use only the first author's last name followed by et al.
options.C: Use the title of the work.
options.D: Use only the last author's name.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: In APA style, what should you do if the source has no author?

options.B: Use a shortened version of the title.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: In APA style, what does "n.d." stand for in an electronic citation?

options.B: Not documented

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: How is the reference list in APA style arranged?

options.B: By date of publication.
options.C: By the order of citation in the text.
options.D: By the title of the work.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a key difference between APA and IEEE textual citations?

options.A: APA uses a numbered list, while IEEE uses the author's name and date.
options.B: APA uses the author's name and publication date, while IEEE uses bracketed numbers keyed to a reference list.
options.C: APA does not require page numbers, while IEEE always does.
options.D: APA uses only the title, while IEEE uses the author's name.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: In IEEE style, what happens once a reference has been listed?

options.B: A new number is assigned each time it is cited.
options.C: The same number is used in all subsequent citations of that source.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is an example of an informational interview?

options.A: A survey you conduct with 100 people.
options.B: An email to a company's general information account.
options.C: Spending time with an expert and asking pertinent questions.
options.D: Reading an article in a journal.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is one of the questions an ethical researcher should ask when evaluating a finding?

options.A: Is this information easy to find?
options.B: Does this finding support my personal bias?
options.C: Is this information accurate, reliable, and relatively unbiased?

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: In the case study about EMFs, what additional question arose after preliminary reading?

options.A: Do townspeople care about the issue?
options.B: Do power lines present the greatest hazard as a source of EMFs?
options.C: How many people live in the town?
options.D: What is the public health manager's job title?

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the importance of a well-defined research question?

options.A: It guarantees an easy research process.
options.B: It guides the entire research work.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further research.
options.D: It ensures the answer will be what you expected.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is one of the things you should skim in a book to gauge the quality and relevance of information?

options.B: A few paragraphs from different portions of the text.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the process of rewriting a passage in your own words while retaining its essence?

options.B: Plagiarizing

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: When using a reference work, what is it important to check to ensure you are accessing the most current information?

options.B: The title

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a key caution about using commercial (.com) or organizational (.org) websites for research?

options.A: They are always biased and should be avoided.
options.B: The information may be affected by an effort to sell something or a particular social/political agenda.
options.D: They do not need to be documented.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is a "conclusive answer" or "ultimate truth" in research?

options.B: The answer that has been proven to be true and agreed upon by all who investigate it.
options.D: An answer that is subject to revision.

questions.unitName: Unit II: Research Process & Evaluation
questions.question: What is the stance on using a Google search for research?

options.A: It should be the only source you use.
options.B: It's fine to start with a Google search to brainstorm ideas, but you will need to narrow down your findings.
options.C: You should never use Google for research.
options.D: It is only useful for academic papers.
